title: GPU node-tier provisioner Terraform module with ASG/Karpenter scale-guard and upgrade hooks
creator: Ava Gupta
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU node 'tiers' for Private (VPC) deployments and supports both ASG-based and Karpenter-based autoscaling. The module should: 1) expose simple tier profiles (e.g., gpu-batch, gpu-rt, gpu-preemptible) that map to instance types, taints, and capacity configurations; 2) implement a "scale-guard" healthcheck and rollout sentinel that prevents node replacement or scale-in when GPU runtime health is degraded; 3) provide plumbing for graceful NVIDIA driver and node agent upgrades with preflight validation and canary lanes; 4) support cross-AZ balancing, spot fallback rules, and drain/cordon hooks that integrate with our runtime drain script and metrics; 5) emit clear Terraform outputs and template consumption examples for Private control plane and customer VPC modules. The module must be usable in both Karpenter-first clusters and ASG-fallback clusters and include opinionated defaults for Private (no public IPs, customer VPC routing).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module publishes variables for tier profiles, instance_families, taints, pod_affinity hints, and autoscaler mode (asg|karpenter)
Scale-guard sentinel implemented as a Kubernetes Job + ClusterRoleBinding invoked by module when lifecycle events occur; scale-in blocked if GPU healthcheck probe fails > 2 minutes
Upgrade hooks: preflight (driver version compatibility check), canary lane (1 node), staged rollout with configurable batch size and grace period
Integration tests: k8s e2e job that simulates driver failure and verifies scale-guard prevents mass termination; ASG and Karpenter CI runs included in pipeline
Module outputs include nodepool_id, instance_profile_arn, iam_role_arn, taint_spec, and example kubeadm labels for control plane consumption
comments: 2026-02-19 - Kickoff: Scoped module boundaries. Decided to support explicit 'tier' profiles rather than freeform maps for easier defaults and discoverability. (Ava)

2026-02-25 - Design review: PM and Runtime reviewed. Agreed to use a lightweight scale-guard that queries DCGM exporter and kubelet readiness instead of a heavyweight controller. Action: Marcus to prototype helm chart that module will deploy.

2026-03-03 - Prototype: Initial Terraform module scaffolding PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6821. Prototype deploys ASG variant and installs scale-guard Job via Helm release. (Marcus)

2026-03-07 - Feedback from Security: Need to ensure IAM role for scale-guard follows least privilege and logs to customer audit sink. Added IAM policy draft link: https://confluence.redwood/priv/infra/iam-gpu-scale-guard

2026-03-10 - Testing: End-to-end test failing in spot-fallback scenario where Karpenter terminates nodes before grace period. Root cause: missing pre-terminate hook. Added drain hook integration and updated acceptance tests. (Sofia)
2026-03-12 - Plan update: Split work into two PRs: (1) module core + ASG support, (2) Karpenter integration + e2e tests. Target merging core by 2026-03-18. (Marcus)
notes: Avoids public IP usage and enforces private subnets by default. Module will include example patterns for both user-managed KMS keys and Redwood-managed keys for driver binaries. Documented migration steps from existing ad-hoc GPU nodegroups. Includes a 'safety_mode' toggle to enable extra preflight checks in high-compliance customers.
implementation_tips: Use terraform locals to materialize tier defaults and allow overrides via map variable for extensibility
Provide a small Helm chart packaged with module to install scale-guard and drain hooks; keep chart values minimal and overridable
Expose lifecycle hooks (pre_terminate_lambda_arn) so customers can plug in extra observability or incident responders
Write e2e tests that run against a dev Private cluster with both ASG and Karpenter enabled; simulate driver crash with forced pod eviction
